listing.description:
cApp is an application framework built around a simple idea: the web application should remain the product. Instead of rebuilding the same experience for every platform, cApp packages and verifies the application, then adds native and local capabilities through explicit contracts.

Applications consume a stable cApp SDK boundary rather than binding themselves directly to a particular desktop shell, mobile runtime or local service. That lets the same product move between ordinary web delivery, installed desktop and mobile builds, and constrained public Showcase demos while keeping product code and platform authority separate.

The framework includes verified capsule compilation and reconstruction, local-first data contracts, native shell profiles, capability-scoped sidecars, on-device Local AI, MCP and agent integrations, hosted-auth handoff, and developer tooling designed to be usable by both people and coding agents.

Developer Showcase and Showroom extend that model into distribution. Verified thin demos and buyer-facing product metadata live in developer-owned public GitHub repositories; cApp keeps only verified discovery pointers. Public project and developer pages are generated dynamically from those contracts and bounded GitHub lifecycle signals.

cApp is currently an alpha-stage V250 standard and also dogfoods itself as a cApp project, making self-hosting, runtime isolation and framework portability part of the product's own test surface.
listing.summary: cApp is a cross-platform application framework for turning an existing web product into browser, desktop and mobile software without maintaining separate product forks. It adds verified packaging, native capabilities, local-first data, Local AI, agent tooling and a GitHub-backed Showcase/Showroom layer.
listing.tagline: One web product. Native runtimes, Local AI, agents and distribution through a stable SDK.
